title: Adaptation labelling sheet
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Ecosystems (7D); atoms, elements and molecules (7H)
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 51 (Adaptation labelling sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 51: Adaptations. To understand how features of organisms help them survive in their environment

picture.draw: Draw and label: Adaptation labelling sheet

questions.q: A fennec fox lives in a hot desert and has huge ears. Explain why.
questions.a: Large ears give a big surface area to lose heat (and to hear prey)
questions.model: Compare with the Arctic fox: small ears keep heat in. The desert is hot, so the fox needs to lose heat. Large ears lose more heat.

questions.q: Why does a cactus have wide shallow roots?
questions.a: To collect rainwater quickly before it evaporates or drains

questions.q: Choose a camel, a fish or a water lily. Draw it and label four adaptations with how each helps.
questions.a: Four correct adaptations with reasons, e.g. camel: hump of fat, wide feet, long eyelashes, can go days without drinking
questions.model: Teacher labels the camel's long eyelashes: 'keep sand out of the eyes in sandstorms'.

questions.q: Design a plant for a dark rainforest floor. Give three adaptations.
questions.a: e.g. large leaves to catch dim light, drip tips, shallow roots

questions.q: Why might an animal well adapted to one place struggle if the climate changes?
questions.a: Its features suit the old conditions; it may not survive the new ones

questions.q: A cactus stores water in its...
Big question: what problem do cactus spines solve?
questions.a: They lose less water than leaves and protect the cactus from animals.
